chapter: Billy Pierce Studio and New York tap
title: What made Slim and Shorty entertaining
summary: They were discovered in the third week; Green explains they were natural entertainers, using comedy, funny mannerisms and the handspring trick.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: So you had been at the studio for how long before you met Buckin' Bubbles?
Well, I was there going into the third week, you see. It was.
So an awful lot happened to you soon as you got to New York.
It did. It really did. Well, Mr. Bradley said this would happen, you know, see. He said we had great personalities, see.
Well, what was it about you and Chuckles that made you have such good personalities? What was it about the way you performed or what you did? Did you do comedy together or --
Yes. Yes.
What kind of things would you do?
Well, we did -- well, my partner, he eventually learned to play the vibraphones, you see, and he did later --
This was prior to the time you were
Chuck and Chuckles -- as Slim and Shorty when you were in Philadelphia, what kind of things would you do that made people like you?

Well, we were so playful, you see. We'd dance, you know, and we made little funny mannerisms, you see. And like I say, I could turn the handspring. See, that was like what you call the punch step, call -- it's actually a trick, you know, of entertaining, you see, and --
That's the word; they were very entertaining, --
Yeah, --
-- because Chuck would play the vibra -- vibes.
Yeah, this was prior to that. He's talking about before.
I mean -- you say you entertained. Now, what -- what was it that gave you the knack to know what was entertaining to people, if you know what I mean?
Well, it's like --
Is this something you were born with?
I guess so. Natural -- natural dancer like, you see.
A flair for comedy?
